why: I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items. Item 1: Check 3 lists the exported functions and fails if "any exported function is not documented in README.md". It also says subtract should be checked specifically. So a README that covers clamp but not subtract would fail, not pass. Item 2: Check 1 compares printed values to an exact string, but every value follows directly from the clamp behaviour in line 1. Check 2 only needs `e instanceof RangeError` and says nothing about the message. Check 3 asks for "its name with its signature or a description of what it does", so no particular README layout is required. Check 4 only needs the tests to pass. The message wording, the exit status and the tests for clamp are all marked advisory, outside PASS/FAIL. No parameter count is required. The builder brief does neither forbidden thing either.
